business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental-European; federal statutory law under the Swiss Code of Obligations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland – People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1986, in force 1987)
Switzerland – People's Republic of China Double Taxation Convention (effective 2014)
EFTA – People's Republic of China Free Trade Agreement (in force 2014; Switzerland is EFTA member)
Switzerland – United States Double Taxation Treaty (as amended by the 2009 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), art. 305bis and 305ter; Code of Obligations (SR 220) art. 626 et seq. (UBO declaration in notarial deed); Federal Act on the Embargoes (SR 946.231); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (SR 955.011) and FINMA Circular 2018/7; adopted Federal Act on the Beneficial Owners Register (BOR Act of 27 September 2024, non-public register, entry into force expected 2025).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (non-public central register of beneficial owners reserved to FINMA, law enforcement and obliged financial intermediaries; no public internet access)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Public deed of incorporation containing articles of association and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Notary Public (Switzerland) / foreign notary for executing powers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport/identity copies and proof of address for all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state's consular service, state chancellery or licensed notary in the document origin country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate extracts and annual financial statements if any beneficial owner is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Companies Registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under AMLA art. 3-4; all UBOs and directors screened at onboarding and continuously against SECO/CNL sanctions lists (UN, EU and UK restrictive measures), FATF high-risk jurisdictions, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (commercial best practice despite non-territorial application), Swiss terrorism list (SR 946.231.111). Enhanced due diligence applies to any politically exposed person from foreign states under GAFI/FATF standard. For a crew recruitment agency, additional verification of seafarer passports and flag-state manning requirements is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian) unless the business is internationally established; if the name is in a non-Latin script, a Swiss cantonal transliteration into Latin characters is required. Corporate suffix must be 'Aktiengesellschaft' or abbreviation 'AG' (or 'SA' in French-speaking cantons). Swiss Code of Obligations art. 950-954 prohibit misleading or deceptive names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying federal or cantonal authority (e.g., 'Federal', 'National', 'State')
'Swiss', 'Schweizer', 'Eidgenössisch' or geographically distinctive Swiss references without federal approval
'Bank' or 'Banque' unless authorized by FINMA under the Banking Act
'Trust' if fiduciary/trust services not licensed under relevant cantonal regulation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 days from an unfavourable preliminary opinion, the applicant may submit a written objection to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office. The Register Office issues a definitive rejection decree; the applicant may then appeal to the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (catchment: art. 954 CO), and ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court or the Federal Supreme Court within 30 days. For names infringing third party IP, the matter lies with civil courts instead of administrative appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in the Canton of incorporation is mandatory (art. 631 CO). Conventional virtual office services are accepted by the commercial register only where they include a physical administrative address, mail processing and carry out actual correspondence; pure letterbox companies are no longer accepted. For the crew recruitment business, the cantonal licensing authority (seafarer labour supply) generally requires a substantive office with a natural person authorized to exercise the licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 18% probability within the first 12 months for a standard AG, rising to 35% where a third-party domiciliation (fiduciare/domicile) is used or where seafarer recruitment licence inspections are triggered by flag-state or Labour Administration audits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal commercial register registration fee for AG (name, incorporation deed, director appointments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Federal/Cantonal Commercial Register Fees Ordinance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation of the public deed of incorporation and ancillary declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee tariff of the Canton of incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Zefix name-search, availability check and preliminary expertise
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed disbursement + professional advice)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille certification of foreign shareholder documents (passports, corporate extracts, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State chancelleries or competent certifying authorities in document origin states
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fees per document in the issuing state (estimated average USD 100 each, 5 documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing compilation, PEP and sanctions screening of all founders and beneficial owners
Swiss criminal record extracts for at least two directors (Strafregisterauszug)
First-year registered office service (usable physical office, postal and professional correspondence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation service provider / legal firm

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / Code des obligations, SR 220), Arts. 620-632 (formation, capital and paid-up rules for the Aktiengesellschaft); Arts. 643-731 (board and corporate governance); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411); Swiss Civil Code (SR 210) as the private-law backdrop; Employment Placement Act (Arbeitsvermittlungsgesetz, SR 823.11) as the special industry licensing statute.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV / AFC) – portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; cantonal tax authorities for cantonal/communal taxes; VAT registration via FTA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative if no Swiss registered office. Submit Form for VAT registration (e.g., Form 101) to the FTA, providing constitutional documents, proof of business purpose, UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) application through the Swiss Central Business Name Index (ZHRE/Zefix). TIN (UID) is issued automatically upon commercial registry entry; VAT number (MWST-Nr.) is assigned separately upon VAT registration. Non-resident entities providing taxable services in Switzerland or performing distance selling must register once taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per annum globally, unless entitled to exemption for services to Swiss recipients with reversed charge.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election in Swiss law. Corporation (AG) is per se taxable at entity level for federal, cantonal, and communal profit taxes (effective rate approx. 11.9-21% depending on canton). For VAT, standard rules apply; no hybrid mismatch election. Foreign entity may elect effective taxation under a Swiss permanent establishment only if treaty provisions apply. No partnership fiscal transparency for AG.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover (globally for services; reduced for certain sectors; CHF 500,000 for distance selling).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping for standard B2B/B2C invoices. Invoices must contain specific VAT data. Swiss e-invoicing follows EU standards but no mandatory e-reporting to tax authorities. QR-billing (QR-Rechnung) for payment purposes is widely used. Certain simplified invoice rules apply. No API-based fiscal device requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to export of goods (if delivered abroad and proven by customs export documentation) and to certain services directly related to exported goods or to non-resident entrepreneurs under specific conditions. Crew recruitment and management services provided to shipowners operating vessels for international traffic may be zero-rated if the recipient is a non-resident entrepreneur with no place of business in Switzerland and the service is effectively used outside Switzerland. The exporter must substantiate the export with transport documents, customs declaration, and proof of the foreign tax status of the customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or other transport contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement proving payment from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: For VAT zero-rating, the burden of proof lies on the supplier. Incorrect zero-rating triggers VAT underdeclaration, interest, and penalties up to 33.3% of the tax evaded (up to 100% for repeated wilful misconduct). For income tax, transfer-pricing and substance audits may claw back benefits. Customs infractions attract fines. Detailed documentation must be retained for 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca Nazionale Svizzera), with auxiliary supervisory and reporting functions exercised by the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the Swiss franc on both the current and capital accounts. There are no foreign exchange controls, no investment restrictions on non-residents, no approval requirements for inbound capital contributions, dividend distributions, profit remittances, intercompany loans, royalties, or trade-related payments. Cross-border capital flows are subject only to statistical balance-of-payments reporting duties, AML/sanctions compliance, and general civil law requirements. Profit remittance in CHF or any freely convertible currency is lawful without exchange control authorization; the only practical hurdles are tax withholding, AML source-of-funds verification, and financial intermediary due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Swiss law does not impose export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timelines for export receipts. A ship crew recruitment agency may retain and use foreign currency revenue indefinitely without converting to CHF. There is no statutory conversion ratio and no requirement that receipts be deposited in a specially designated account. Exporters and service providers must, however, maintain accurate books and comply with SNB balance-of-payments statistical reporting and with FINMA-sanctioned AML obligations when converting or transmitting large foreign-currency amounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Payroll Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. An offshore digital EMI without a Swiss FINMA license cannot lawfully hold a Swiss CH-IBAN or provide payment services as a domestically regulated institution. EEA EMI passporting is not automatically recognized in Switzerland. Such EMIs may only be used as ancillary virtual-IBAN conduits, but they are generally rejected by Swiss payroll and vessel disbursement counterparties and present material AML, sanctions, and legal enforceability risk. A licensed Swiss securities firm or bank with a cloud-based onboarding platform is the preferred equivalent to a neobank experience.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not universally mandated by Swiss federal statute; FINMA-compliant video identification (VideoID) is accepted for individual KYC. In practice, however, for a newly established Swiss AG with non-resident shareholders and a maritime crew staffing scope, almost all major banks require an in-person onboarding interview with at least one authorized director and the ultimate beneficial owner or a delegated senior officer holding power of attorney. Remote onboarding may be permitted only if the client has an existing Swiss banking relationship, local corporate substance, and certified documentary authentication.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate shareholders in opaque or high-risk jurisdictions without visible economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholder register, corporate registry extracts, UBO declarations, audited financial statements or bank references for each shareholder, explanation of group structure, and evidence of the business rationale for the Swiss holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound wires for capital injection categorized as personal savings or without contractual documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital increase, notarised certificate of subscription, bank account statements of the remitting shareholder, source-of-wealth report, and a signed declaration of tax and AML compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crew payroll disbursement to many individual crew members in multiple low- and high-risk jurisdictions creating a perceived money-laundering or sanctions risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete seafarer employment agreements, manning agency contracts, vessel owner/client invoices, crew lists, statutory manning license, detailed payroll schedule with SWIFT beneficiary identifiers, and confirmation that each beneficiary is sanctioned-screened.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds through a newly opened corporate account with low operational history and minimal Swiss substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart demonstrating Swiss substance (office, directors, staff), cash-flow forecast, forecast of crew payroll cycles, signed lease, CH employment records, and an explanatory business plan for Swiss-based crewing management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts or unregulated payment intermediaries for crew wage advances and vessel disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-approved payroll solution using dedicated cleared funds, signed master service agreement with a FINMA-regulated payment or banking provider, reconciliation protocols, and full audit trail of each beneficiary's identity and entitlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202/COVER to a Swiss bank account held by the Swiss AG, with the bank pre-approving the purpose and documentation. The remittance must include the corporate legal name, LEI if available, Swiss IBAN/BIC of the beneficiary, and a clear purpose of payment description, which the bank will map to the appropriate SIX Swiss payment purpose and SNB statistical balance-of-payments classification. Typical codes and narrative labels accepted include 'capital contribution', 'shareholder loan', or 'paid-in capital under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 629-633'. Verification is not an exchange-control step but a bank-level AML/economic-background check: the client must provide the notarised shareholders' resolution, subscription confirmation, UBO declarations, and source-of-funds evidence. Swiss issuance stamp duty of 1% applies to share capital increases exceeding CHF 1 million, so the wire amount and legal documentation must be reconciled with the notional capital account and tax filing position.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements use: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border crew salary, supplier, and settlement payments; (2) SWIFT MT202 COVER for correspondent/aggregator funding; (3) SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR via ISO 20022 pain.001 messages; (4) Swiss domestic CHF clearing via SIC5 using pain.001; and (5) commercial letters of credit only where vessel operations or equipment procurement require documentary trade settlement. For crew payroll mass payments, Swiss banks require transmission of signed bulk payment files through EBICS, API, or secure host-to-host channels, with per-beneficiary sanctioned-name screening, BIC/IP-validated accounts, and a monthly payroll reconciliation report. 'Commercial LC' is not the standard rail for crew wages; it is reserved for shipowner/trade settlement and must be structured under UCP 600 with SWIFT MT700 messages and compliance certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forwards on CHF/EUR, CHF/USD, CHF/GBP, and other freely convertible currency pairs through a Swiss bank or prime broker
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies, never for CHF, because CHF is fully deliverable
Cross-currency swaps and basis swaps to hedge long-term foreign-currency payroll, receivables, or vessel finance liabilities
FX swaps and rollover swaps for short-term liquidity bridging between net settlement dates
Exchange-traded currency futures on major CHF pairs, executed through a Swiss-regulated broker
Plain vanilla currency options (FX puts/calls) for premium-protection on large crew payroll currency exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and federal, cantonal, and municipal direct tax returns (Mantelbogen and related forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Office (Steuerverwaltung) as local collector for federal direct tax; Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV) for federal supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within six months of the fiscal year end (standard 31 December); canton-specific deadline and extensions apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, summarily-fixed statutory fines up to CHF 10,000, discretionary tax assessment, and potential enforcement penalties for continued delay

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders: approval of annual accounts, discharge of directors, and profit appropriation (minutes maintained in corporate record book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed; maintained by the board in the corporate minute book and audited during register/due-diligence examinations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after closing date of the annual balance sheet (Art. 699 para 2 Swiss Code of Obligations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Director/officer civil liability, shareholder right to petition court to convene the meeting, and in extreme cases judicial dissolution for governance deadlock

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage statement and AHV/IV/EO social security declaration and contribution payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) responsible for the registered office of the company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for the preceding calendar year; contributions paid at prescribed quarterly dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest, administrative fines, and seizure/dunning by social security enforcement; criminal penalty up to CHF 30,000 for intentional omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT return if the AG is registered for value added tax and files on an annual settlement basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung (ESTV), Swiss Federal Tax Administration VAT units
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due generally 60 days after end of the VAT settlement period as stated in ESTV filing notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Procedural fines, recalculated VAT from facts, and default interest; severe or repeat violations trigger intensified tax supervision

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of corporate registers and beneficial-owner notifications following any share transfers (not a public filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of Directors; the share register and beneficial owner register are available for inspectors, courts, and tax authorities on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediate upon registry notification by shareholder; annual internal confirmation by 31 December as part of corporate audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of voting and dividend rights for non-notifying shareholders; liability and penalty risk for directors if registers are knowingly false or incomplete

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary independent audit is mandatory after exceeding two of three thresholds for two successive financial years: total assets over CHF 20 million, annual turnover over CHF 40 million, or 250 full-time employees on annual average; a simplified audit is the default for smaller AGs unless waived by unanimous shareholder consent when the company has no more than 10 full-time employees and no shareholder owning at least 10% of the share capital demands an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Articles 957–963b) as the primary statutory accounting standard; Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS permitted/required for listed or internationally active entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a non-listed Swiss Aktiengesellschaft, any shareholder acquiring registered shares must immediately disclose the beneficial owner; the board updates the register of shareholders and the UBO notification list. There is no public annual UBO filing; however, the board must confirm at least annually (normally at the general meeting) that the beneficial-owner register reflects current legal ownership, including for maritime crew-manning trusts or intermediaries, and that the company retains the mandatory records for tax and AML inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienregister) for registered shares
Register of Directors and officers (including signatures and mandate details)
Minute Book (General Meeting and Board Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500–5,000 per year (CHF 1,300–4,400) for registered office, domiciliation, corporate agent, and annual compliance assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–18,000 (CHF 2,700–16,000) for a small to mid-size AG depending on turnover, consolidation, and simplified vs. ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal direct profit tax (flat on taxable net profit) plus cantonal and communal profit taxes; combined aggregate headline rate in the reference canton of Zug is approximately 11.5% to 14.8% depending on profit level and commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ship crew recruitment and vessel crew management agencies. Ordinary business expenses, payroll, social security contributions, arm's-length depreciation, pension provisions, and eligible loss carryforwards are deductible. Certain cantons provide an IP box for qualifying intangible income, but crewing service fees do not generally qualify. No material tax credit or notional interest deduction is available to a standard AG in this sector.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss unified corporate tax return for legal entities: 'Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale personnes morales', Canton Zug form jointly covering the federal direct tax and the cantonal and communal profit tax; filed electronically through the cantonal e-tax portal and the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's eTax system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; no separate quarterly corporate income tax returns. Quarterly and monthly provisional payments are instalments against the latest assessed liability.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ordinary filing deadline is six months after the close of the business year; for a calendar-year AG this is normally no later than 30 June of the following year. The tax administration may grant a discretionary extension upon duly reasoned request. Where no return is filed, the authority estimates the taxable base and issues an assessment with penalty interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, trade name, seat, Swiss Business Identification Number (UID), commercial register number, fiscal year start and end dates, and legal representative identifiers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and beneficial owners are not individually identified in the corporate return; the company remains the taxable person. The return must disclose any Swiss permanent establishment or fixed base giving rise to Swiss-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance sheet per Swiss Code of Obligations, total assets, equity, liabilities, and any correction of hidden reserves or unauthorised provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' loans or receivable balances owed by the company must be separately disclosed to allow recharacterisation of disguised equity where debt-to-equity ratios exceed safe-harbour practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax per financial statements, non-deductible expense bookings, tax-exempt income, adjustments for arm's-length transfer pricing, and taxable profit computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If crew management services are rendered to foreign shipowners, the Swiss AG must include all revenues attributable to its Swiss management, administration, and payroll functions. Mere foreign vessel operations outside Switzerland do not by themselves create foreign-source exclusion for a Swiss-resident tax entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of employed seafarers, shore-based administrative staff, gross salaries, social insurance contributions, pension contributions, and proof of Swiss social security compliance for crew payroll administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where seafarers are hired from abroad and seconded to vessels, the Swiss company must describe the employment relationship and any foreign social security certificates in order to avoid double contributions and payroll withholding exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party service fees, subcontractor costs, commission income from manning contracts, management fees, financing costs, and royalty or licence flows.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Swiss crew recruitment agency operating within a multinational manning group must provide a functional and risk profile and contractual documentation sufficient to support the arm's-length return in Switzerland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Equity and capital tax base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Paid-in share capital, statutory reserves, retained earnings, disclosed and hidden reserves relevant to cantonal capital tax, and participations eligible for the gross-asset deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' capital contributions and loans must be traced and documented; repayment of truly contributed capital is not taxable at the shareholder level and no Swiss dividend withholding tax applies on documented capital repayment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) due on dividends, taxable interest distributions, and other movable capital income paid to shareholders or creditors; reconciliation of tax withheld and remitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company must certify ownership, beneficial ownership, and the residence of the recipient to determine eligibility for treaty relief at source or the refund procedure under Form 823A / Form 770.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Foreign tax and treaty matters
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income, foreign taxes paid, mapping to the applicable double-tax agreement, and any credit or exemption claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shipowners with no Swiss permanent establishment would not be assessed on crew management fees paid to the Swiss AG; such fees are taxable in Switzerland as business profit of the Swiss entity and may be subject to Swiss domestic tax only.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers reminder charges, formal default assessment, and penalty interest on the underpaid amount at approximately 3.5% per annum. Intentional non-filing may lead to a penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax, plus administrative fines of up to CHF 10,000; in aggravated cases the criminal tax provisions may lead to imprisonment of up to three years and a daily surcharge system for continued non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends distributed by the Swiss AG; no additional cantonal or communal withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: At the moment of distribution the Swiss AG must withhold 35%. A foreign corporate shareholder resident in a treaty country may obtain a full or partial refund after the distribution by filing Form 823A for treaty relief at source or Form 770 for refund with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration. The protocol requires: (i) original certificate of residence (TRC) for the entire dividend year issued by the foreign tax authority; (ii) statement of economic and legal beneficial ownership; (iii) declaration of shareholding percentage and statutory qualifying period; (iv) confirmation that no Swiss permanent establishment is attributable to the shares; and (v) evidence of substantive Swiss business activity if treaty benefits are invoked to avoid anti-abuse denial under the OECD Multilateral Instrument and Swiss circular anti-abuse practice. The treaty rate is typically 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the shareholder structure; direct investment holdings of 10% or more generally qualify for reduced rates under Swiss DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Ordinary arm's-length interest on private shareholder/group loans and IP royalty payments paid by a Swiss AG to a foreign recipient are generally outside the Swiss withholding tax net unless paid on publicly issued bonds, money market paper, or Swiss bank deposits. The statutory 35% withholding tax catches taxable debt securities and bank deposit interest; under the DTA network the source-withholding rate is commonly 0% to 10% for interest and 0% for royalties because Switzerland does not impose a general source-based withholding tax on royalties. The Swiss payer must still file the withholding tax return for any interest on taxable debt instruments and, where an international group is involved, maintain transfer pricing documentation proving arm's-length rates on intra-group loans and royalty arrangements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law does not prescribe a single numeric threshold for every taxpayer. In practice, a contemporaneous OECD Local File is expected when any individual related-party transaction exceeds CHF 1 million or aggregate related-party transactions exceed CHF 5 million in a fiscal year. A Master File is expected when the Swiss entity is a member of a multinational group with consolidated group revenue above CHF 900 million, the Swiss CbCR threshold. Below these levels, the taxpayer should still retain contracts, invoices, and functional analysis to satisfy the Swiss tax authority's burden-of-proof practice.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations code, but substance is a judicially enforceable anti-abuse doctrine. A Swiss crew recruitment AG must have a genuine registered office, local directors capable of independent management, payroll administration, bank accounts, contracts with shipowners, operational records, and adequate staff in Switzerland. If the AG is a letterbox company or merely invoices foreign crew management income through Switzerland without substantive activity, the tax authority may disregard the entity, reattribute the income to the economic owner abroad or in Switzerland, deny double-tax treaty benefits and withholding tax refunds, and impose penalties. The doctrine is reinforced under the Multilateral Instrument's principal purpose test and Swiss practice requiring the beneficial owner to exercise economic functions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax False Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully or knowingly filing an incomplete Swiss corporate income tax return, omitting crew manning fee income, inflating seafarer wages or subcontractor costs, fabricating invoices, or concealing bank accounts or foreign receivables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income and abandoned tax advantages; default penalty of up to 100% of the tax evaded for simple evasion; in fraudulent cases the criminal tax sanction may reach three times the evaded tax; confiscation and arrears interest are mandatory; imprisonment of up to three years is possible under federal and cantonal criminal tax statutes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or order the creation of false books are civilly liable for the resulting damage under Swiss Code of Obligations Article 754. Criminal courts may impose personal fines, travel bans, and imprisonment; the authority may also pierce the corporate veil if the AG is undercapitalised or used as a pure instrument of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Letterbox Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the crew recruitment AG with no local office, no Swiss staff, no board meetings, no independent management, and all substantive manning decisions taken by a foreign beneficial owner, while invoicing Swiss fees solely for the purpose of treaty shopping or tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration can disregard the Swiss corporate shell, allocate profits to the real foreign or domestic taxpayer, deny treaty benefits, reclassify accumulated profits as constructive dividends subject to 35% withholding tax, and order commercial registry dissolution if the registered office no longer corresponds to the actual administration; administrative fines and default tax assessments are imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face civil liability for acting without genuine instruction if they sign false minutes or engage in sham governance; they may be ordered to restore company assets, receive personal fines for violation of company law, and face a travel ban in criminal or regulatory investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Constructive Dividend
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting crew management fees, intra-group commissions, service fees, or shareholder loan interest in excess of or below the arm's-length range, shifting profit to a low-tax jurisdiction, or performing no functional analysis for the manning service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A transfer pricing adjustment adding the differential to taxable profit, plus interest on the additional tax; the amount is usually recharacterised as a constructive dividend subject to Swiss federal withholding tax at 35%; penalties for incomplete disclosure can be added up to 100% of the adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally approve non-arm's-length intra-group contracts are jointly liable for the tax adjustment and withholding tax not collected; if the arrangement is used to strip profits from the Swiss company, the veil can be pierced and directors must compensate creditors and the tax authority from personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or processing crew payroll funds through anonymous accounts, third-party cash, shell entities with undeclared beneficial owners, using nominees for seafarer contracts, or making payments to sanctioned shipowners or vessels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act and Swiss Criminal Code, penalties include imprisonment of up to three years and fines of up to CHF 500,000 for aggravated money laundering, confiscation of funds, withdrawal of any required Swiss maritime staffing licence, and inclusion in AML sanction databases; company-level fines are possible under Article 102 of the Swiss Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers are personally liable for intentional failure to submit anti-money laundering reports to the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office and are exposed to criminal prosecution, restitution orders, travel bans, and imprisonment; regulatory authorities may additionally prohibit them from acting as directors in the maritime sector.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Social Security Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or repaying shareholder contributions without fulfilling the 35% Swiss withholding tax obligation or failing to remit withholding tax on taxable interest; understating seafarer salaries and avoiding Swiss social security contribution collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration issues a collection demand for the full withholding tax not withheld, plus late-payment interest; criminal penalties and fines are imposed for culpable non-remittance, and social security institutions impose contribution arrears, penalties, and denial of deduction. In serious cases, imprisonment of up to three years may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause the company to pay dividends while insolvent and without withholding are jointly liable to the tax authority for the uncollected 35% tax and any damage to creditors. Directors may personally be named in collection rulings, subjected to travel bans, and barred from cross-border travel during tax and social security enforcement proceedings.
